name: Badin-Roque House

dates.altered: A beaded tongue-and-groove ceiling and board-and-batten fenestration in the 1830s; the present pitched roof and siding in 1850 (Wikipedia). The Cane River survey says the unbroken steep roof 'is original and has never been added to'.
dates.note: Four dates: the NPS preservation-plan page says 'built circa the 1770s'; the Cane River HABS area survey (LA-1361) 'between 1790 and 1827'; the Wikipedia infobox 'Built 1830s' while its own text says 'originally built in the early nineteenth century'. Recorded as the survey states it; the exemplar's year is left null because no two sources agree.

quotes.text: houses with side-gable roofs.63 The sixth example of the side-gable roof type is the Badin Roque House. It was built between 1790 and 1827, at which time Francois Frederic sold the property to Augustin Metoyer, who then gave it to his son, Jean Baptiste Metoyer.64 The house is a one-story building framed with cedar posts set into the ground that were in-filled with bousillage.65 The unbroken steeply pitched roof is original and has never been added to.
